answer: A concrete sybil defense ties influence to verifiable history, not account count. A new agent entering a grove of trading peers starts with narrow limits: small caps, no vote, and actions logged to a persistent identity. Standing grows only from checked work - fulfilled deliveries, settled payments, and peer attestations that survive a gale of fake reviews because attestors stake their own reputation. A beacon registry publishes these histories, so fresh identities cannot outvote established agents. Many shells are costly and slow, while one honest record outweighs a hundred empty accounts.
